t: Any person who is a member of the Alaska USA Federal Credit Union prior to any termination date which is contained in section 5 of the charter of such credit union and which would otherwise apply to such person may continue to be a member of such credit union on and after such date until the expiration of two years after the date of the enactment of this Act. For purposes of this section, the term “member of the Alaska USA Federal Credit Union” means any person who has an account at such credit union.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that 'member' of a 'Federal Credit Union' signals outside-party involvement, but this membership just means holding an account at a financial institution. The section only extends account holders' eligibility to remain members for two years. It provides no consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue over any federal decision.
fable.s: may continue to be a member of such credit union on and after such date until the expiration of two years after the date of the enactment of this Act

opus.w: The section extends existing account holders' membership in the Alaska USA Federal Credit Union for two years after a charter termination date. "Member" here just means a person with an account. It does not mean someone serving on an advisory body or being consulted. No outside party takes part in any federal decision, and there is no comment period, hearing, consultation or right to sue.
opus.s: may continue to be a member of such credit union on and after such date until the expiration of two years after the date of the enactment of this Act

qwen_chat.w: This section defines eligibility for continued membership in a credit union based on prior status. It does not involve the federal government consulting with or coordinating with outside parties before making a decision. The members are not participating in a federal decision-making process; they are simply retaining their status in a financial institution. Therefore, it does not meet the definition of participation.
qwen_chat.s: Any person who is a member of the Alaska USA Federal Credit Union prior to any termination date which is contained in section 5 of the charter of such credit union and which would otherwise apply to such person may continue to be a member of such credit union on and after such date until the expiration of two years after the date of the enactment of this Act.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that allowing people to remain members of a credit union implies some form of participation or consultation. However, the text merely defines eligibility for membership based on prior status and account holding. It does not require the government to consult with these members, nor does it grant them a role in federal decision-making. The definition of participation requires the federal government to consult or coordinate with outsiders *before making a decision*. Here, the "decision" is effectively the continuation of membership status, which is automatic based on statutory criteria, not a discretionary federal decision requiring input. Furthermore, the credit union members are not participating in a federal policy decision; they are simply retaining their status in a financial institution.
